thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU serving pool 'inference-europe-1' queue length > 14k, sustained 5m. Throttled requests rising, autoscaler attempted but hit node cap. Detected recent deploy: continuous-batching:v2 (config change: prefix_cache_size reduced from 40GB->8GB). Possible KV cache missstorm.

erin_oncall: Acknowledging. Paging in. Observed 502/429 spike for hosted customers and increased tail latency. Which jobs rolled this out?

sam_sre: rolling deploy started 1791231400 by ci/cd pipeline (maria_ml's change). Autoscaler logs show scale-up requests rejected with "quota_exceeded: max_gpus=20" at 1791232702. Pool already at 18/20 GPUs.

maria_ml: I merged the batching PR, it changed continuous batching heuristics and lowered prefix cache retention to free memory for larger kv cache entries. I can revert but need a quick mitigation first.

incident-bot: RUNBOOK NOTE: if autoscaler hits cap, either increase pool cap or reduce per-worker memory to allow more replicas. See runbook: /runbooks/gpu-capacity-exhaustion.md

erin_oncall: Steps: 1) Open temporary burst-cap (if possible), 2) revert batching config OR disable continuous batching, 3) flush prefix cache to rebuild, 4) notify customers. Who can do step 1 now?

sam_sre: I can request a temporary soft-limit bump with infra. Requesting now: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed set-autoscaling --max-num-replicas 30 --zone europe-west1-b --target mypool` -- but infra approval needed for quota increase. Pinged infra.

maria_ml: I’m rolling a hotfix to revert prefix_cache_size to 40GB from the deploy branch. Will push a rollback to canary-only first. Command:

```bash
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/worker CONT_BATCHING_CONFIG=continuous-v1
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/worker PREFIX_CACHE_SIZE=40GB
```

maria_ml: Pushing canary now (1791233005).

taylor_prodeng: If canary looks good, do a fast rollback across the pool but staggered to avoid a thundering rebuild of caches. Use 10% steps.

jaime_support: Customer impact: Monitoring dashboard shows ~120 accounts with increased latency and ~5 customers with elevated error rates (including enterprise-cust-42). Raising a priority outbound to account reps.

sam_sre: Infra responded: can increase soft cap to 28 GPUs immediately; hard quota needs org approval (takes 6-8h). Applying soft bump to 28 now.

incident-bot: ACTION: autoscaler max_gpus changed from 20 -> 28 at 1791233422 (temporary). Observe queue.

erin_oncall: After bump we still see queue slowly decreasing, but tail latency still high. Looks like workers are thrashing due to prefix cache misses and KV refill overhead. Need to reduce continuous batching to lower memory churn.

maria_ml: Disabling continuous batching on non-critical routes to cut memory pressure. Command: `kubectl -n inference patch deployment worker -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"worker","env":[{"name":"CONT_BATCHING_ENABLED","value":"false"}]}]}}}}'` (applied to 20% of replicas at 1791233600).

sam_sre: Also increasing worker restart grace to allow cache warmup: `kubectl -n inference set env deployment/worker CACHE_WARMUP_TIMEOUT=120s` (applied).

incident-bot: METRIC SNAPSHOT: queue_length 5m avg went 14k -> 3.2k after bump+canary rollback; throttle_rate down 73% -> 18%. Error rate for top enterprise-cust-42 still elevated (10x baseline).

jaime_support: Notifying customer success & account reps: sent initial summary and mitigation ETA. They requested an incident update for SLA exposure. Drafting now.

taylor_prodeng: Long-term we should add safety checks in the batching config change: don't reduce prefix cache size below X% of model KV size, and tie autoscaler target to per-worker memory footprint. Filing a ticket.

maria_ml: Canary rollback looks stable. Rolling full rollback in 5% steps with 60s between batches.

sam_sre: Watcher: still seeing a small pool of workers with repeated KV eviction logs: `WARN kvcache: evicting prefix key due to memory_pressure` at 1791233802. These workers are responsible for many long sequences -> amplify cache misses.

erin_oncall: For any remaining hot customers, we can route to a compatible model variant with lower KV requirements (model-small) as fallback. Planning to enable routing policy for 10 affected tenants. Approval?

maria_ml: Approved. Updating routing rules: `redwoodctl routing set --tenant enterprise-cust-42 --model model-small --duration 2h` (done at 1791233945).

incident-bot: NOTIFICATION: Paging on-call for follow-up if error rate > 5% for another 30m.

jaime_support: Sent update to affected customers: summary of incident, mitigation steps taken (autoscaler soft-cap bump, rollback of batching config, temporary routing fallbacks), and expected full recovery timeline ~1.5h.

sam_sre: Queue at 1791234200: 900 -> continuing downward. Throttle_rate ~6%. Marking service degraded but functional.

erin_oncall: Postmortem TODOs: - Add pre-deploy guardrail in CI for prefix_cache_size vs model_kv_size - Autoscaler should surface when cap is hit earlier to UI - Add runbook step to stagger cache warmups - Improve metric alerting to correlate KV eviction spikes with error rate.

maria_ml: Will open PRs for guardrails and feature flags to avoid automatic large memory reductions in future.

taylor_prodeng: Closing pager now? Any objections?

jaime_support: Ok to close from support side; customers notified.

erin_oncall: Closing pager at 1791234888. Will start postmortem doc and link to rollback commit + autoscaler event logs.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED by erin_oncall at 1791234888. Summary: regression from batching/prefix-cache change caused KV cache misses -> worker memory pressure -> autoscaler hit cap -> queue growth/throttling. Mitigations: temporary soft-cap bump, canary rollback of batching config, disable continuous batching on non-critical routes, routing fallbacks for impacted tenants. Action items assigned.
